question.problem:
Suppose we would like to find the minimum value of the function $f(x,y,z)=x+{y}^{2}+z$ on the intersection of the surfaces $3{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=2$ and $x+{z}^{2}=1$ using the method of Lagrange multipliers. Then, the corresponding Lagrange multipliers $\lambda $ and $\mu $ satisfy the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}⟨1,\,2y,\,1⟩=\lambda ⟨0,\,\bbox[2pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}},\,2z⟩+\mu ⟨1,\,\bbox[2pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}},\,2z⟩ \\ 3{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=2 \\ x+{z}^{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

From left to right, what are the missing expressions?
question.worked_solution:
We need to find the minimum value of 

$$
f(x,y,z)=x+{y}^{2}+z
$$

 

subject to the constraints 

$$
g(x,y,z)=3{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=2,\,h(x,y,z)=x+{z}^{2}=1.
$$

Therefore, by the method of Lagrange multipliers, we must solve the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z)=\lambda ∇g(x,y,z)+\mu ∇h(x,y,z) \\ g(x,y,z)=2 \\ h(x,y,z)=1\end{aligned}
$$

We now expand the first equation of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\lambda ∇g(x,y,z)+\mu ∇h(x,y,z) \\ ⟨{f}_{x},{f}_{y},{f}_{z}⟩ & =\lambda ⟨{g}_{x},{g}_{y},{g}_{z}⟩+\mu ⟨{h}_{x},{h}_{y},{h}_{z}⟩ \\ ⟨1,\,2y,\,1⟩ & =\lambda ⟨0,\,6y,\,2z⟩+\mu ⟨1,\,0,\,2z⟩\end{aligned}
$$
